ai.description: This lizard reaches 25 cm in length. It is olive-brown with a pale throat and a prominent, serrated crest running from the nape down the back. A distinct black patch marks the side of the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Coryphophylax subcristatus* is best distinguished by its prominent, continuous nuchal crest of elongated scales, which is significantly more developed than in other Indian agamids.
ai.habitat: The Nicobar Forest Dragon inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Nicobar Islands, typically found on tree trunks at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Nicobar Forest Dragon is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or rocks to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Coryphophylax subcristatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Coryphophylax subcristatus* is endemic to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, inhabiting lowland tropical forests from sea level up to approximately 200 meters.
